note: Lesson is mostly rule-talk on awal / akher / taani / ghair / nafs with translation drills; several rows are his offered forms that Amal rejected with 'Nothing' - kept as voiced grammar. The 1:04:01 goodbye line lost its b- in BOTH his and her line, so it reads as the engine. ghair rows are engine Latin ('qayril yom').

row.why: He used the noun تأخير (delay) for the adjective متأخر (late); at 08:35 Amal voiced his sentence back as إنت صحيت متأخر and he repeated أنا صحيت متأخر at 08:39 - a voiced recast, not chat only (the brief's own TR-18 example uses this exchange).

rulings.why: Voiced recast at 08:35 that he repeats at 08:39; late but it restates his own sentence with the fixed word, so A not B.

row.medi_said: And if I say الأول الساعة, that means the f-- the, the... I thought you said this was also the first hour
row.amal_said: Nothing. ... It would be the first if the أول is after. صح.
row.why: He put el-awal before the noun to mean 'the first hour'; Amal said it means nothing and the adjective must come after (الساعة الأول -> أولى at 18:36) - the noun + adjective order rule, A7; offered while talking about the rule, so medium.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; her fix is the adjective-after rule, which is A7, not a new bucket.

row.medi_said: and التاني الساعة means a different hour.
row.amal_said: لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything. ... It follows it, بس without the ال.
row.chat: taani saa3a = second hour / second hour
row.why: He put el- on تاني in front of الساعة; Amal said it means nothing and at 22:08 that it follows the rule 'without the ال' - the front word never takes el- (A2); offered as his reading of the rule, so medium.

rulings.why: Her stated fix (22:08 'without the ال') is the front-word-takes-no-el rule, A2.

row.chat: awal el-sa3a = the b eginning of the hour.
row.right: أول اليوم = the beginning of the day
row.proposed_rule: awal / aa5er + an el- noun means the beginning / end of it (أول اليوم = the beginning of the day); awal + a bare noun means the first (أول يوم).
row.why: In her guessing drill he read أول اليوم as 'the first day' twice; she repeated أول اليوم at 30:37 and 30:41 until he said 'The beginning of the day' at 30:52.

rulings.why: Real listening misread fixed by her repeated prompt; no bucket covers the awal + el- = beginning rule, so PROPOSE.

row.medi_said: الأول الـ اليوم / الأول اليوم. No, that's the-- Isn't that the first day?
row.why: He offered الأول اليوم for 'the first day'; Amal said 'Nothing' twice and gave اليوم الأول, and he said 'Oh, that's right' - adjective goes after the noun (A7).

rulings.why: He himself says 'Isn't that the first day?' and accepts اليوم الأول, so the right piece is اليوم الأول (not أول اليوم) and the rule is A7.

row.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Uh, هذا الثاني. (engine wrote هذا الثاني; her echo shows حدا التاني)
row.amal_said: حدا التاني is / no. X. Just حدا تاني.
row.why: Her echo shows he said حدا التاني (engine wrote هذا الثاني): el- on the adjective after an indefinite noun; she said 'no. X. Just حدا تاني' - noun + adjective el- placement, A7.

rulings.why: Clear voiced no with echo; the fix is where el- sits in noun + adjective, which A7 covers, so no new bucket.

row.proposed_rule: غير (other / different) goes straight before a bare noun and never takes el- after it: غير يوم, not غير اليوم.
row.why: Reading back her بشوفك غير يوم he said 'qayril yom' (with il-), as at 38:11; she recast غير يوم at 39:18 (and 38:12) - engine Latin, so the il- may be a linking vowel, hence low.

rulings.why: He keeps adding il- after ghair and she recasts each time; no bucket covers ghair + bare noun, so PROPOSE, low because the line is engine Latin.
